$comment: Pinned expected-case denominators for every devnet-validate suite.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (#953, same class as #945/#923): every suite in this
harness reports N/N by counting the rows it produced. A stimulus that never
fires produces no row, so N/N is tautological — '26/26 adversarial' said
nothing about whether 26 cases ran. A denominator is only meaningful when it
comes from OUTSIDE the run that produces the numerator.
Every count here is checked in two directions:
hard-fails below it, and records status='short' in the JSON).
2. scripts/test-denominators.sh asserts these counts still match the
scripts on disk, so adding a script without bumping the pin fails CI-
style verification rather than silently widening the gate.
Bump a number here only together with on-disk evidence of the new count.

cli_parity.$comment: One row per tx-zoo/09-cli-parity/09*.sh. EQUAL+DIVERGENT+SKIP+ERROR must sum to this. Env-skips are counted as their own class and never folded into EQUAL.

n2n_adversarial.$comment: Rows in n2n-trace.csv. NOT the same as the count of adv_record call sites (28) — two sites are mutually-exclusive branches. Confirmed live: see the closing evidence on #953.

chaos.$comment: One terminal row per chaos/*.sh (excluding lib.sh). ENV-SKIP is a counted class, never silence (#959).

parity_matrix.$comment: The parity denominator is per-invocation (it depends on which categories were requested), so it is carried in parity-matrix.meta.json written by bidirectional-parity.sh. This block pins the categories the STANDARD gate must cover, so a run that quietly narrows its category list fails the gate.
